title: NHS: Missed or late periods
keywords: late period missed periods menstrual cycle irregular causes stress weight exercise contraception pregnancy
content: A late or missed period can happen for many reasons, including pregnancy, stress, sudden weight loss, being overweight, too much exercise, or some forms of contraception. If pregnancy is possible, a pregnancy test can help clarify the cause. Contact a healthcare professional if you are concerned, miss periods repeatedly, or have other symptoms.

title: NHS: Doing a pregnancy test
keywords: pregnancy test pregnant late missed period when test
content: Most pregnancy tests are most reliable from the first day of a missed period. If you do not know when your next period is due, test at least 21 days after unprotected sex. Follow the instructions that come with the test.

title: NHS: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
keywords: pcos polycystic ovary syndrome irregular periods acne hair fertility diagnosis
content: PCOS is one possible cause of irregular periods, but irregular periods can have many causes. A healthcare professional assesses symptoms and may arrange tests; a late period alone cannot establish that someone has PCOS.

title: NHS: Period problems
keywords: period pain heavy bleeding period problems doctor healthcare professional
content: Period problems can have different causes. Seek medical advice if period pain or bleeding is severe, affects daily life, or is a change from what is usual for you. Sudden severe pain or very heavy bleeding may need urgent assessment.
